reason: Almost always frames the inscription or image field ("Inschriftfeld von Halbsäulen eingefasst", "links des Inschriftfeldes eine tordierte Halbsäule"), and framing architecture never counts (docs/annotationsrichtlinien.md, Abschnitt 1); no column is annotated in the goldstandard or the test set. Stopped for all three methods, Methode 3 included, since 2026-09-25 (Lisa) - until then Methode 3 kept a column unless a "von"-PP under a framing verb framed the inscription field, which missed "flankiert", "links des Inschriftfeldes" and the image field. Earlier reason: "Säule" is structurally ambiguous: almost always frames the inscription field/monument (not a depiction), occasionally frames the image field itself or stands next to a depicted figure (a real element then) - see docs/edh_methoden.md, "Stopliste-Auflösung". Regex/Lemmatisierung drop it outright; Dependency Parsing resolves it via framing_verbs/framed_targets below.

"Altar" is structurally ambiguous: most EDH mentions describe the monument itself ("Mittelteil eines Altars", "Altar oder Statuenbasis" - the inscription's own carrier, not a depiction), a minority describe an actually depicted altar within a Bildfeld/Fries/Relief ("In unterem Bildfeld Altar mit Flamme", "Reste eines Frieses mit Reiter und Altar") - see docs/edh_methoden.md. Regex/Lemmatisierung drop it outright (shared stoplist exclusion); Dependency Parsing keeps it only if it shares a dependency component (see sentence_components() in dependency.py) with one of requires_context below - validated against all 4 goldstandard true positives and all 6 false positives found during fine-tuning.

"Person(en)" is mostly about the people named in the inscription ("Anzahl der genannten Personen", "Bestattungsdaten der drei beigesetzten Personen"), only sometimes about depicted people ("Darstellung zweier Personen", "Brustbildern dreier Personen") - checked against all ~70 Person/Personen mentions in the corpus 2026-09-23, see docs/edh_methoden.md. Regex/Lemmatisierung drop it outright; Dependency Parsing keeps it only if it shares a dependency component with one of requires_context below.

"Turm" in EDH commentary is almost always a findspot or building ("im Kirchturm vermauert", "des Alten Turms"), not a depiction - 0 of 27 corpus mentions share a dependency component with a depiction word (tested 2026-09-24). Kept in the vocabulary so the element is searched in every source; Regex/Lemmatisierung drop it outright, Dependency Parsing keeps it only with one of requires_context below.

Methode 1's substring search finds "tisch" in every adjective on -tisch ("identisch", "keltisch", "hypothetisch" - 85 comments, 5 real "Tisch"), too many to list as false friends. Methode 2/3 match the noun lemma and are unaffected. Decided 2026-09-24.

Methode 1's substring search finds "rad" in "Grad", "gerade", "Balustrade", "retrograd" and names ("Radnóti", "Radimský") - 44 hits, none a depicted wheel. Methode 2/3 match the noun lemma and are unaffected. Decided 2026-09-24.

"Tafel" in EDH commentary is almost always the inscribed carrier itself ("Von der Tafel sind 3 Fragmente erhalten"). Of 377 sentences with "Tafel", the 8 that describe a depicted tablet all use "halten": the inscription tablet held by erotes/genii ("Die Tafel wird von Eroten gehalten" - the same motif as EDB "genius tabellam tenens") or writing tablets in a figure's hand. Regex/Lemmatisierung drop it outright, Dependency Parsing keeps it only with "halten" in the same dependency component. Checked 2026-09-24.

"Kreis" in EDH commentary is mostly a shape description ("halbkreisförmig", "kreisrund", "Kreises") rather than a depicted circle. Regex/Lemmatisierung drop it outright, Dependency Parsing keeps it only with a depiction word in the same component. Decided 2026-09-24.

"Kopf" is mostly an idiom in EDH commentary ("Kopf- und Fußende" of a tomb, "auf den Kopf gestellt") or the preserved part of a figure. Counted only with a person or a depiction word in the same dependency component (18 of 70 corpus mentions, all real depicted heads, tested 2026-09-24); it is then the portrait form "head" (portrait_head_*), like "Büste" for bust. Regex/Lemmatisierung drop it outright.

"unbestimmt"/"unbestimmbar" are everyday words in EDH commentary ("unbestimmter Herkunft"); they only point to an unidentified depicted object next to a signal word. Regex/Lemmatisierung drop them outright. Decided 2026-09-24.

Methode 1's substring search finds "tier" in "Datierung" (362x), "zitiert", "dokumentiert", "datiert" and other verbs on -tieren - far too many for false friends. Methode 2/3 match the noun lemma ("Stier" goes to bull, the longer form). Decided 2026-09-25, when "Tier" was added after the test-set measurement.

"Bogen" in EDH comments is almost always the architectural frame or the shape of the monument ("Nische mit Rundbogen", "Rundbogenstele") - framing architecture never counts (docs/annotationsrichtlinien.md, Abschnitt 1), and no arch is annotated in the goldstandard or the test set. Stopped for all three methods, Methode 3 included (no context rule). Decided 2026-09-25; a truly depicted arch is left to later methods (docs/spaeter.md).

Like column: pilasters in EDH comments frame the inscription or image field ("Inschriftfeld von Pilastern eingefasst", "auf den Pilastern zu Seiten des Inschriftfeldes"); framing architecture never counts and no pilaster is annotated in the goldstandard or the test set. Stopped for all three methods, 2026-09-25 (Lisa).
